steps.title: Prepare H1 minimal medium (200 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following reagents in distilled water to a final volume of 200 mL: 2.24 g K₂HPO₄ (11.2 g L⁻¹), 0.96 g KH₂PO₄ (4.8 g L⁻¹), 0.40 g (NH₄)₂SO₄ (2 g L⁻¹), 4 g NaCl (20 g L⁻¹), 1 mL 1 M MgSO₄·7H₂O (1 mM), and 0.10 mL 0.5 % (w/v) FeCl₃·6H₂O (1.85 µM). Autoclave the solution; after cooling, add the MgSO₄ and FeCl₃ solutions (marked * in the recipe).

steps.title: Prepare supplemental solutions
steps.instruction: Make three separate solutions: (a) Yeast‑extract 10 % (w/v) by mixing 2 g yeast extract in 20 mL distilled water; (b) Glycerol 75 % (v/v) by mixing 75 mL glycerol with 25 mL distilled water (total 100 mL); (c) Saline 2 % (w/v) by dissolving 2 g NaCl in 100 mL distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare agar plates
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 % (w/v) bacteriological agar to the H1 minimal medium (with either 3 % glycerol for accumulation or 0.25 % yeast‑extract for non‑accumulation), autoclave, pour into sterile glass Petri dishes, and let solidify.

steps.title: Inoculate fresh plates and start overnight culture
steps.instruction: Spread a fresh H1 minimal medium plate containing 0.25 % yeast extract with the desired strain (e.g., Halomonas titanicae KHS3) and incubate at the appropriate temperature until colonies appear. Pick a colony and inoculate 3 mL of the same medium; incubate overnight.

steps.title: Inoculate main cultures (50 mL)
steps.instruction: Transfer the overnight culture into a 250 mL flask containing 50 mL H1 minimal medium to obtain an initial OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.05. Use accumulation medium (H1 + 3 % glycerol) for PHB‑producing cultures or non‑accumulation medium (H1 + 0.25 % yeast extract) for controls. Grow with shaking at the strain‑specific temperature, monitoring OD₆₀₀ periodically.

steps.title: Determine culture volume for PHB assay
steps.instruction: When the culture OD₆₀₀ reaches the desired sampling point, calculate the volume needed to obtain 2 mL of cell suspension with OD₆₀₀ between 1.7 and 2.0 using the formula: (2 mL × desired OD) ÷ (current OD) = volume to harvest. Example: for OD₆₀₀ = 0.45, harvest 7.55–8.90 mL.

steps.title: Harvest cells and resuspend
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the calculated culture volume at 9 700 × g for 5 min. Discard the supernatant, gently remove residual liquid with a P200 pipette, and resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of 2 % NaCl solution (or, for non‑halophilic strains, an appropriate low‑ionic buffer).

steps.title: Aliquot cell suspension for assay
steps.instruction: Divide the 2 mL resuspended cells into two 700 µL aliquots in 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes. Label one tube “dH₂O” and the other “NaClO”.

steps.title: Add reagents for NaClO assay
steps.instruction: To the “dH₂O” tube add 150 µL distilled water; to the “NaClO” tube add 150 µL of 5.5 % (w/v) sodium hypochlorite (household bleach). This yields a final NaClO concentration of 1 % (w/v) in the assay tube. Gently mix each tube to homogenize.

steps.title: Incubate assay tubes
steps.instruction: Incubate both tubes at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Measure optical density
steps.instruction: After incubation, gently homogenize each tube again and measure OD₆₀₀ within 15 min. Record the values for the water‑treated and NaClO‑treated samples.

steps.title: Calculate % PHB (dry weight basis)
steps.instruction: Use the OD₆₀₀ readings in the formula provided in the Data Analysis section of the original article (e.g., %PHB = [(mg PHB · mL⁻¹)/(mg cells · mL⁻¹)] × 100).

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: Rodríguez et al. [3].
